Acceptance_question: Does every active facility have one stable internal identifier that is not its display name?
Pass_criteria: One immutable identifier maps to the current name and every legacy name
Required_evidence: Facility identity register plus source-owner approval
Failure_example: A rename creates a second facility
First_remediation: Create the stable identifier and a legacy-name crosswalk
Review_trigger: Any rename move merge split closure or acquisition

Acceptance_question: Are facility building floor zone and unit modeled as different types?
Pass_criteria: Each record has one declared type and containment relationship
Required_evidence: Approved type dictionary and sample hierarchy
Failure_example: A gate lane is treated as a rentable unit
First_remediation: Separate spatial classes and rebuild the relationship

Acceptance_question: Can the team distinguish an asset from the record describing it?
Pass_criteria: Physical asset and source-system record have different identifiers
Failure_example: Replacing a keypad erases the old device history
First_remediation: Separate the device identity from the vendor record

Acceptance_question: Are display names treated as labels rather than join keys?
Pass_criteria: No operational join depends only on free-text name
Required_evidence: Query or export showing stable-key joins
Failure_example: North Annex and River Campus split one history
First_remediation: Replace name joins with governed identifiers

Acceptance_question: Does every changing relationship have an effective start and an open or explicit end?
Pass_criteria: Temporal fields are present and timezone is declared
Failure_example: A vendor appears responsible before its contract starts
First_remediation: Add effective-dated relationship records

Acceptance_question: Are active inactive retired closed and unknown distinct states?
Pass_criteria: State dictionary defines allowed values and evidence for each
Failure_example: Missing data is treated as closed
First_remediation: Add Unknown and require state evidence

Acceptance_question: Can each critical fact name the source that asserted it?
Pass_criteria: Source identifier is mandatory for critical assertions
Failure_example: A dashboard label has no origin
First_remediation: Add source reference and quarantine orphan assertions

Acceptance_question: Is the source allowed to assert that fact?
Pass_criteria: Source-authority matrix maps fields to authoritative roles or systems
Failure_example: A vendor portal renames the enterprise facility
First_remediation: Remove authority and route a correction

Acceptance_question: Are observation event decision authorization and work represented separately?
Pass_criteria: The five classes cannot be collapsed into one status row
Failure_example: A motion signal is treated as approved dispatch
First_remediation: Split the record into typed nodes

Acceptance_question: Are person role and role assignment separate?
Pass_criteria: A person may hold dated roles without changing identity
Failure_example: An employee transfer rewrites prior approvals
First_remediation: Model effective-dated assignments

Acceptance_question: Does every authorization point to the role and policy that allowed it?
Pass_criteria: Authorization has actor role policy scope and time
Failure_example: AI confidence is treated as approval
First_remediation: Require a human or system authority record

Acceptance_question: Can a derived fact name the activity and inputs that generated it?
Pass_criteria: Derived assertion links to transformation version and source assertions
Failure_example: A metric has sources but no transformation version
First_remediation: Record generation activity and inputs

Acceptance_question: Does correction supersede rather than silently overwrite?
Pass_criteria: Prior assertion remains addressable and new assertion cites it
Failure_example: Wrong unit mapping disappears without trace
First_remediation: Append a superseding assertion

Acceptance_question: Are vendor IDs scoped to their issuing system?
Pass_criteria: Every external identifier includes namespace and effective period
Failure_example: Two vendors both use location 101
First_remediation: Add issuer namespace and validity dates

Acceptance_question: Can one work order affect multiple assets without implying one asset identity?
Pass_criteria: Work-to-asset relationship supports one-to-many and preserves each asset
Failure_example: One work order merges two doors into one device
First_remediation: Model separate affected-asset edges

Acceptance_question: Is evidence distinct from the conclusion it supports?
Pass_criteria: Evidence artifact and assertion or decision use separate IDs
Failure_example: A photograph is treated as proof of completion by itself
First_remediation: Require a signed or system-attested conclusion

Acceptance_question: Are required types fields cardinalities and allowed values executable?
Pass_criteria: A versioned validation rule set produces a report without mutating inputs
Failure_example: The glossary exists but invalid records enter production
First_remediation: Implement pre-release validation

Acceptance_question: Are closed-world operational requirements stated separately from open-world inference?
Pass_criteria: Critical workflows have explicit completeness shapes or checks
Failure_example: No approval record is interpreted as approval not needed
First_remediation: Define mandatory evidence and fail closed

Acceptance_question: Is entity equivalence an approved assertion rather than a similarity inference?
Pass_criteria: Every merge has evidence approver effective time and rollback
Failure_example: An AI similarity score auto-merges two facilities
First_remediation: Route match candidates to review

Acceptance_question: Can the system answer what was believed and effective at a past time?
Pass_criteria: Valid time and recorded time are both queryable
Failure_example: A late correction rewrites last month's operating view
First_remediation: Add effective and observed or recorded timestamps

Acceptance_question: Can vocabulary and data versions evolve independently?
Pass_criteria: Ontology version validation version and data snapshot are separately identified
Failure_example: A rule change makes old records silently nonconformant
First_remediation: Pin versions and migrate explicitly

Acceptance_question: Are sensitive relationships excluded or access-controlled by design?
Pass_criteria: Data classification and least-necessary graph views are enforced
Required_evidence: Access policy and redacted test export
Failure_example: Unit and access data leak into public structured data
First_remediation: Separate internal and public graphs

Acceptance_question: Can the system distinguish model output from authoritative fact?
Pass_criteria: Every model assertion carries model version confidence evidence and disposition
Failure_example: Predicted equipment identity becomes master data
First_remediation: Label as proposed and block direct promotion

Acceptance_question: Can downstream consumers prove they received an approved change?
Pass_criteria: Each release has target status timestamp and exception state
Failure_example: A corrected facility name reaches the dashboard but not access control
First_remediation: Add consumer acknowledgments and exceptions

Acceptance_question: Is the ontology tested against named operational questions?
Pass_criteria: Every release answers a governed query suite
Failure_example: The graph is rich but cannot find open work for a retired asset
First_remediation: Define competency questions before classes

Acceptance_question: Are identifiers persistent collision-resistant and owned?
Pass_criteria: Namespace policy assigns minting ownership and never reuses retired IDs
Failure_example: A deleted unit ID is reassigned to another unit
First_remediation: Prohibit reuse and create successor relationships

Acceptance_question: Are inferred and asserted relationships separately inspectable?
Pass_criteria: Named graphs or equivalent scopes preserve origin and inference regime
Failure_example: Inferred containment is exported as source fact
First_remediation: Tag graph and rule provenance

Acceptance_question: Can a bad ontology or mapping release be reversed without deleting evidence?
Pass_criteria: Release manifest links prior version migration and rollback procedure
Failure_example: A class merge corrupts production joins
First_remediation: Restore prior graph and quarantine migration

Acceptance_question: Are query and validation budgets measured without weakening controls?
Pass_criteria: Named workloads have bounded test environments and failure handling
Failure_example: Validation is bypassed when volume spikes
First_remediation: Partition or queue validation while preserving gates

Acceptance_question: Can the team explain who may add deprecate or reinterpret each term?
Pass_criteria: Change process requires owner rationale impact review version and effective date
Failure_example: One analyst repurposes closure to mean unavailable
First_remediation: Govern term changes through review

Acceptance_question: Can core concepts be exported without exposing provider-specific internals?
Pass_criteria: A neutral export maps local terms and preserves limitations
Failure_example: Vendor field names become the enterprise ontology
First_remediation: Create a provider-neutral canonical layer

Acceptance_question: Can a retired system leave without erasing identity lineage?
Pass_criteria: Source records remain referenced or archived with durable provenance
Failure_example: A migration removes the evidence behind old work
First_remediation: Archive governed snapshots and mappings
